purpose: Determine whether the same pinned LaMa checkpoint can reconstruct a greater-than-1024-source-pixel hole without resizing the source.

tests.limits: The complete 2048 combined probe failed during output writing; numerical parity was then verified by separate runtime/reference commands. Report-only memory_scope fields added after the 1024 regression.

observations: Native 2048 ONNX export retains all 989 learned generator tensors and 36 Fourier units from pinned source/checkpoint; no trained weights changed.
Official-version ORT CPU inference completes, with finite shape-correct native 2048 output and <=1 SDR code difference from upstream PyTorch.
Runtime-only peak RSS is about 7.6 GiB and inference about 147 seconds on this shared host.

100-percent diagnostic inspection shows a broad smooth fill and lost plausible market structure in the selected hole. This is a visible challenge failure, not a numeric release score or proof about all scenes.
Known SDR source pixels outside the rectangle are byte-identical in the diagnostic composite.

First combined reference/runtime run exhausted disk while saving output. Only this task's rebuildable Xcode intermediates were removed; apps, evidence, model/source artifacts and originals retained. Separate runs completed afterward.
remaining: No canonical scene-linear RAW input, HDR/seam/noise or saved-patch/export qualification at 2048.
No exact app C-API/dylib, GPU provider, iOS, browser or lower-memory physical-device test at this extent.
The model and current application remain unqualified for large-object release; no pin, runtime admission, schema, ABI, generation limit or provisioning change.
